title: The Verification

canonical_node.axiom: The kernel does not grade its own homework, and neither do we.
derivation: 0 axioms, 4 assumptions, 3 definitions, 17 theorems, 0 sorry in the Lean kernel.
All load-bearing commitments are carried as structure fields on AxiomBundle, so every theorem displays its dependencies.
The four assumptions are destructive_degrades, good_preserves, good_alignment_is_moral, moral_good_repairs_damage.
Seventeen theorems are proved with zero sorry, including mercy_restores, grace_restores, veto_collapse, and both_positive_imply_positive.
Three bridges are declared open with kernelProved := false and status := openBridge.
canonical_node.action: Treat the four AxiomBundle assumptions as the entire attack surface; treat the seventeen theorems as the only machine-checked claims; treat the three open bridges as unfinished work requiring explicit derivation or theological identification, not as theorems.
boundary: Does not claim the four assumptions are proven; they are assumptions.
Does not claim the open bridges are closed; they are labeled open.
Does not claim the /Mathlib port is complete; it is pending.
Does not claim the definition-ablation matrix for the Maxwell coupling is complete; it is remaining work.
test: Check that the keyword 'axiom' does not appear in the kernel source.
Check that the four assumptions are the only assumptions in the AxiomBundle structure.
Check that all seventeen theorems compile with zero 'sorry'.
Check that the three open bridges have kernelProved := false and status := openBridge.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a machine-checked inventory of the formal kernel: zero axioms, four assumptions, seventeen theorems, and three open bridges, establishing a single visible attack surface.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the distinction between machine-verified claims and theological identifications, and maintains the honest labeling of open work.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If this sheet is removed, the framework loses its authoritative list of what the kernel actually proves, allowing unverified claims to be mistaken for verified ones.
dg5_translation_registers: axiom count: 0 kernel axioms, 4 bundle assumptions, 38 spine axioms (proposed), ~188 axiom-tagged ledger rows (inventory)
open bridges: 3 (Lagrangian-to-product form, maximal coherence identified with Christ, global uniqueness of coherence fixed point)

classification.recommended_atom_action: preserve as canonical inventory; do not upgrade open bridges to theorems

overstatement_risks: Treating the four assumptions as proven facts rather than assumptions.
Treating the three open bridges as closed theorems.
Treating the /Mathlib port as complete when it is pending.
Treating the Maxwell coupling invariant as fully verified when the definition-ablation matrix is remaining work.
kill_conditions: If the keyword 'axiom' appears in the kernel source, the zero-axiom claim fails.
If any of the seventeen theorems contains 'sorry', the zero-sorry claim fails.
If any open bridge is presented as a theorem without explicit derivation, the honesty protocol fails.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the three open bridges or explicitly mark them as non-theological, and complete the /Mathlib port.

plain_summary: This sheet is the authoritative inventory of the Lean 4 formal kernel: zero axioms, four assumptions, three definitions, seventeen theorems, and three open bridges. It establishes the attack surface and the honest labeling of unfinished work. The claims are machine-checked for the core, but the  port and some ablation work remain pending.
